correctness.rationale: For an increasing partial injection, f²=0 exactly when ordered domain and image are disjoint. The original two-sided fence characterization reduces to matching adjacency-gap flags and parity of corresponding entries. Each map of rank floor(n/2) leaves at most one unused point, making both domain and image run-length compositions identical. The zero-hole and one-hole run-seam case split is exhaustive: no seam gives alternating runs, while the unique equal-color seam reverses paired-block orientation. Counting even compositions or compositions with one odd part gives the displayed top-stratum formulas. Odd cardinalities in both parity classes rule out full rank at n≡2 (mod 4), with explicit constructions attaining all bounds. A standalone script independently enumerated all square-zero maps up to n=13 and reproduced ranks and claimed top counts. n≡2 counts are not claimed.

originality.rationale: The direct monoid-defining papers give the map criterion, semigroup generator rank, ideals and maximal subsemigroups; these are explicitly credited. The closest published whole-monoid rank enumerator does not impose disjoint domain/image, so it cannot directly count square-zero maps. A multipartite graph-isometry theorem has a different admissibility condition and factorial multiplicities. A contraction theorem optimizes nilpotency index rather than square-zero rank. The run-bijection top-stratum formulas were not found in actual published-finding corpus and public literature searches; this is a best-evidence originality assessment, not absolute-priority certification.

value.rationale: Square-zero elements form the natural nilpotency-index-two stratum of an inverse transformation monoid. The sharp rank loss on exactly one residue class is not predictable from the ambient rank limit alone, and the explicit exponential saturated counts require analyzing synchronized domain/image run compositions. These classify infinitely many extremal strata with distinct mod-four structure, while clearly leaving one exceptional multiplicity open. The result is more informative than recomputing monoid size or a small finite table.
